questions.note: Order reads right: hallux longest, toe 2 a few mm short. Toe 2 now has a PIP knuckle, a waist and a pulp from above, but from below it wears a cuff ledge; the hallux from below is a straight-sided box with no sulcus or pulp dome and in profile a shallow paddle; both knuckles carry one stamp of even grooves and toe 2's DIP crease is a knife cut.

In scope both nails read as press-on French-tip acrylic: a tile in an even gutter under one uniform rim, a crisp white proximal sliver for a lunula, a constant-width ivory free edge with a squared slab corner and stacked wavy stripes, a highlight that washes the plate white, no grime. The pink bed now shows; free-edge thickness is visible but slab-like.

Nothing to score as relief: the dorsum above the hallux and toe 2 is smooth and oily, with no EHL cord onto the hallux, no extensor slip to toe 2 and no veins, so nothing catches the rim light; the saphenous vein is out of these frames.

SSS holds: shadow sides stay dark, no glow. But the micro-relief is a crumpled-cellophane crackle, the pads carry straight corduroy ridges with no whorls, the skin under the free edge is blurred and the web shadow smeared, and the colour is one clean salmon with an oily sheen: it reads as a silicone prosthetic.

defects.what: The hallux plate is a rounded-rectangle tile set in an even gutter inside one uniform raised rim, its side edges standing proud as bevels with no lateral fold rolling over them: a press-on nail; toe 2's is the same tile.
defects.fix: Real lateral folds rise over and hide the plate's edges and the proximal fold is a soft roll of varying width with a thin cuticle; let the plate sink under the folds and vary the rim.

defects.what: Both free edges are constant-width opaque ivory bands with a crisp bevelled rim and a wavy white stripe inside, the same on the hallux and toe 2: an acrylic French tip.
defects.fix: A clipped toenail's free edge is a narrow, slightly uneven band, faintly yellow-grey and translucent at the rim, varying in width along the cut, with a faint grime line beneath.

defects.what: From below the hallux is a straight-sided rounded box growing straight out of the ball: no toe-base sulcus, barely an IP crease, no oval pulp dome wider than the shaft.
defects.fix: The underside folds deeply where the toe leaves the ball, the proximal pad and the pulp are separate swellings across a clear IP flexion crease, and the pulp is an oval dome wider than the shaft.

defects.what: Under toe 2 a crisp ledge with a white seam rings the toe at the PIP crease, smooth and pinker above, ridged below, the outline stepping out with flaps at both ends: a thimble pushed on.
defects.fix: A plantar flexion crease is a soft transverse fold across continuous skin, the same colour and ridges on both sides, the outline only dimpling where it ends.

defects.what: The friction ridges are straight parallel stripes at one diagonal angle over the ball, the hallux pad and toe 2, crossing the creases unbroken; at native size they read as corduroy moiré.
defects.fix: Ridges form whorls or loops centred on each pulp, arcs across the toe bases and transverse flows on the ball, and stop at the flexion creases.

defects.what: The hallux IP and toe 2 PIP wrinkles are one stamp: three or four identical, evenly spaced, full-width glossy grooves with bright lips that notch the profile like comb cuts (clearest in the medial view).
defects.fix: Knuckle skin bunches into short, broken creases of unequal depth, length and spacing, densest over the joint centre and fading at the sides, different on each toe.

defects.what: The lunula is a crisp-edged bright white sliver pressed against the proximal fold, and toe 2 carries the same white arc: a reverse French stripe or an exposed plate edge, not a soft pale half-moon.
defects.fix: The hallux lunula is a dull, milky crescent about 3.5 mm deep with a soft, slightly irregular distal border, partly under the fold; on toe 2 it is faint or hidden.

defects.what: The 1–2 web ends in a ruler-straight horizontal margin that meets toe 2's medial wall almost square: a shelf between the toes, also seen in the hallux view.
defects.fix: Seen from the front a web margin is a soft U, curving from the hallux's side into toe 2's, with a shadowed fold and fine wrinkles.

defects.what: In profile the hallux is long, shallow and flat, under 18 mm deep at the nail root and tapering to a tongue with the nail riding on it like a cap: a paddle rather than a blunt, deep big toe.
defects.fix: Keep the dorsum high to the nail root and let the pulp hang as a rounded bulb under the nail; Jeff's direction puts the depth at about 25 mm at the IP.

defects.what: The hallux and toe 2 are bald in every view: no tuft of dark hairs on the hallux's proximal phalanx and none on toe 2.
defects.fix: 8–12 dark brown hairs, 5–8 mm, lying flat distally on the hallux's proximal dorsum; 2–4 hairs of 3–6 mm on toe 2's proximal phalanx.

defects.what: The dorsum above the hallux and toe 2 is a smooth, oily surface: no EHL cord running onto the hallux, no extensor slip to toe 2, no dorsal veins.
defects.fix: The EHL stands as a cord over the first MTP onto the proximal phalanx and catches the rim light; the slip to toe 2 is a fainter ridge; veins are low relief.

defects.what: A thin raised glossy line arcs across the first MTP dorsum at the hallux's base and cuts two notches into the medial profile: it reads as a healed incision.
defects.fix: If it is meant as the MTP's dorsal crease, make it broad, shallow, interrupted and matte, without a raised lip; otherwise remove it.

defects.what: Toe 2's DIP crease is one long even groove with a bright lip across two thirds of the toe, a knife cut, its end breaking into white flecks.
defects.fix: Two or three short, shallow, soft creases of unequal length fading out at the sides.

defects.what: In the highlight the micro-relief breaks into sharp, angular, randomly oriented facets like crumpled cellophane, the same crackle crisp on every dorsal surface.
defects.fix: Skin micro-relief is fine furrows in two or three dominant directions bounding soft rhomboid plateaus; it breaks a highlight into a fine, even sheen, not foil-like glints.

defects.what: Below the hallux free edge the pulp and hyponychium skin are blurred and featureless while the side wall beside them carries a crisp crackle: detail sharp in one place, waxy in the next.
defects.fix: The pulp carries the toe's finest, densest relief (ridges at about 0.45 mm), as sharp at this scale as the side wall.

defects.what: The plate's highlight washes half the hallux nail to near-white with soft vertical combing, so the plate reads as polished white acrylic.
defects.fix: Keratin shows a smaller, softer sheen broken by faint, uneven longitudinal ridges, with the bed's pink still visible around and through it.

defects.what: The free edge's lateral corner is a squared, thick slab end with a flat cut face resting on the skin.
defects.fix: A trimmed toenail corner is slightly rounded, thinner toward the side and dips into the lateral fold.

defects.what: Above the free edge a wavy white band, a thin pink line and the free edge's own wavy border repeat the same regular wave in parallel, like stacked lacquer layers.
defects.fix: One soft onychodermal band, a slightly darker pink-brown line with an irregular, non-periodic border, then the free edge.

defects.what: From below, toe 2's free edge shows past its pulp as a glassy sliver with a puckered rim, and the hallux's free-edge corners glint past its pulp.
defects.fix: With nails trimmed short the pulp hides the free edge from below, or shows it only as a thin opaque line.

defects.what: In clay the hallux free edge sits over a crescent pocket with a crisp rim concentric with the edge, as if the plate were seated in a carved cup.
defects.fix: The hyponychium meets the free edge in a shallow, soft distal groove, the pulp swelling up to it unevenly.

defects.what: In the shadowed web recess the micro-relief vanishes and the skin breaks into soft blotches, like denoiser smear at 64 samples.
defects.fix: Enough samples, or a gentler denoise, that the relief and the web's fine creases hold into the shadow.

defects.what: In clay a tiny bright fleck under the hallux free edge suggests the plate's underside pokes through the hyponychium.
defects.fix: Keep the plate's underside clear of the hyponychium surface under the free edge.

ranked: [D1] The hallux nail, the focus of most views, is a press-on: a rounded-rectangle tile in an even gutter inside one uniform raised rim, its side edges standing proud as bevels with no fold rolling over them; toe 2's nail is the same tile in miniature.

[D2] Both free edges are constant-width opaque ivory bands with a crisp bevelled rim and a wavy white stripe inside: an acrylic French tip. A clipped toenail's edge is narrow, uneven, faintly yellow-grey, with a grime line under it.

The skin is one clean, even salmon from dorsum to tip, with no capillary redness on knuckles and tips, no darker creases, no blue-grey cast on the hallux dorsum, and an oily sheen on the dorsum and web: it reads as a silicone prosthetic.

[D3] From below the hallux is a straight-sided rounded box that grows straight out of the ball: no toe-base sulcus, barely an IP crease, no oval pulp dome wider than the shaft; it reads as a glove's thumb, not a weight-bearing toe.

[D4] Under toe 2 a crisp ledge with a white seam rings the toe at the PIP crease, smooth and pinker above, ridged below, the outline stepping out at both ends: the distal part looks like a thimble pushed on.

[D5] The plantar ridges are straight parallel stripes at one angle over the ball, both pads and the phalanges, crossing the creases; at native size they read as corduroy moiré. Real pads carry whorls or loops and arcs, broken by the creases.

[D6] The hallux IP and toe 2 PIP wrinkles are one stamp: three or four identical, evenly spaced, full-width glossy grooves that notch the profile like comb cuts. Knuckle skin bunches into short, broken creases of unequal depth.

[D7] The lunula is a crisp, bright white sliver pressed against the proximal fold, and toe 2 has the same white arc: a reverse French manicure rather than a dull milky half-moon with a soft border, faint or hidden on toe 2.
[D8] The 1–2 web ends in a ruler-straight horizontal margin meeting toe 2's wall almost square, a shelf between the toes; a real web is a soft U with a shadowed fold and fine wrinkles.

[D9] In profile the hallux is long, shallow and flat, under 18 mm deep at the nail root and tapering to a tongue with the nail riding on it like a cap: a paddle, not the blunt, deep big toe of a grown man.
[D10] The hallux and toe 2 are bald in every view: no tuft of dark hairs on the hallux's proximal phalanx, nothing on toe 2; with the clean skin this is the mannequin read.
[D11] The dorsum above both toes is smooth and oily: no EHL cord onto the hallux, no extensor slip to toe 2, no veins, so the forefoot shows no structure under its skin.
[D12] A thin raised glossy line arcs across the first MTP dorsum at the hallux's base and cuts two notches into the medial profile; a podiatrist reads a healed incision, not a crease.
Nothing ages the hallux: no pinch callus or dry patch on its medial side, no thickened or yellowed nail, no scuffs. A boot-wearing 40-year-old's big toe looks worn; this one looks freshly cast.
[D13] Toe 2's DIP crease is one long, even groove with a bright lip across two thirds of the toe, a knife cut, where real skin shows two or three short soft creases fading at the sides.

[D14] Up close the micro-relief is a crumpled-cellophane crackle of sharp angular facets, crisp and alike on every dorsal surface; in a highlight it glints like foil instead of spreading into a fine, even sheen.
[D15] Below the hallux free edge the pulp and hyponychium are blurred and featureless while the side wall beside them carries a crisp crackle: detail sharp in one place, waxy in the next.

[D16] The highlight washes half the hallux plate to near-white with soft vertical combing, like polished acrylic; keratin shows a smaller, softer sheen broken by faint uneven ridges, with the bed's pink around it.
[D17] The free edge's lateral corner is a squared, thick slab end with a flat cut face resting on the skin, where a trimmed nail's corner is slightly rounded, thinner and dips into the lateral fold.

[D18] Above the free edge a wavy white band, a thin pink line and the edge's own wavy border repeat the same regular wave in parallel, like stacked lacquer layers, not one soft, irregular onychodermal band.
[D19] From below, toe 2's free edge shows past its pulp as a glassy sliver with a puckered rim, and the hallux's free-edge corners glint past its pulp.

[D20] In clay the hallux free edge sits over a crescent pocket with a crisp rim concentric with the edge, as if the plate were seated in a carved cup rather than meeting the pulp in a soft distal groove.
[D21] In the shadowed web recess the micro-relief vanishes and the skin breaks into soft blotches, the look of denoiser smear at 64 samples.
[D22] In clay a tiny bright fleck under the hallux free edge suggests the plate's underside pokes through the hyponychium.
